business: Soul Studio — a yoga and Reformer Pilates studio at Crnogorskih Serdara 45, Podgorica; the page's single job is to let someone who has never done either practice tell them apart and then message the studio on Instagram or call.
artDirection: Warm bone-and-clay editorial calm: a body-temperature paper ground, near-black warm ink, one terracotta accent, and a high-contrast Bodoni display face used at genuinely large sizes against a quiet Manrope text face. The direction is "the room, transcribed" — the studio's actual architecture (a lit arch in the back wall) and its actual painted wall motto become the page's two structural devices, so the identity is borrowed from the premises rather than invented in Figma. Nothing glows, nothing floats, nothing is a card; the page is flat planes, hairlines, and four photographs, and every decorative move can be traced to something physically present in the studio.
signatureElements: The arch crop (page.tsx:156, `rounded-t-[14rem] rounded-b-sm`). The hero photograph is cut into an arch that mirrors the illuminated arched alcove visible *inside that same photograph*. It is declared in the code comment as the only rounded crop on the page, which makes every other square edge read as deliberate restraint rather than default. This one shape carries the whole brand.

The wall motto as the largest type on the page (page.tsx:223-234, data.ts:23). "Move the body / Open the heart / Feed the soul" is literally painted on the studio wall and photographed in the gallery frame below. It is set at clamp(1.75rem, 6vw, 3.25rem) in Bodoni, one line per <li>, each preceded by a hairline — larger than the H2 that introduces it. The copy beside it explicitly refuses to claim it as a slogan: "Nije slogan — to je redoslijed po kojem se radi." English inside a Montenegrin page is justified because that is the language on the wall.

Signature-under-headline inversion (page.tsx:114-126). The H1 ("Pokret. / Disanje. / *Prisustvo.*") leads the column; the category descriptor "YOGA & REFORMER PILATES · PODGORICA" sits *below* it under a hairline, so it reads as a signature on a piece of work rather than the standard eyebrow-pill-above-heading opener. The third H1 line is italic and clay — the only colored word in the headline.

Self-drawing hairlines and bottom-up photo uncover (soul.module.css:29-69). Two scroll-driven CSS animations, no JavaScript, no IntersectionObserver: `.rule` scales X from 0 with `transform-origin: left`, `.reveal` animates `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` upward — described in the file's comment as "light crossing the floor." Both use `animation-timeline: view()` behind `@supports` + `prefers-reduced-motion`, so an unsupporting browser gets the finished page, not a blank one.

The deliberately uneven photo grid (page.tsx:44-49, 266-284). A `Record` keyed by photo `src` (not array index, enforced by `as const satisfies`) assigns each frame its own cell span and box height: the tall wall-lettering frame owns a full column via `sm:row-span-2`, two squarish frames stack beside it, and the landscape hall shot closes with `sm:col-span-2`. The code comment names the enemy: "A 2×2 of identical tiles is the grid this page is trying not to be."

The mobile action dock as a pill, not a bar (page.tsx:375-403). A floating rounded rectangle inset from all edges with an asymmetric `grid-cols-[1.55fr_0.75fr]`: a filled clay cell showing a two-line Instagram label ("PIŠI NAM" over the truncated handle) and a smaller outlined Pozovi cell. Solid ground, no blur — the comment cites the house ban on glassmorphism — and the page carries matching `pb-[calc(6rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]` so nothing hides behind it.

The unloaded map plate (MapEmbed.tsx:51-79). Instead of an iframe, a `currentColor` repeating-linear-gradient grid at 15% opacity draws a map plate with zero assets and zero requests to Google until the visitor presses a real button — and it inherits whichever palette the demo uses.
typography:
Two families only, split by job and documented as such at page.tsx:11-13: Bodoni Moda (`--font-soul-display`) for every heading, hero, and the motto — \"Bodoni's hairlines are the whole point at display sizes and unreadable below them\" — and Manrope (`--font-soul-sans`) for all running text, nav, eyebrows, and buttons; both loaded with `latin-ext` for č/ć/š/ž/đ. There is exactly one shared H2 clamp, `clamp(1.9rem,4.5vw,3rem)` / `2.75rem`, reused across all four section headings, so the page has a real scale rather than per-section improvisation; the H1 (`clamp(2.75rem,9vw,5rem)`, `leading-[0.98]`, `tracking-[-0.02em]`) and the motto (`clamp(1.75rem,6vw,3.25rem)`, `leading-none`) are the only two things allowed above it. Hierarchy comes almost entirely from three levers — size, weight-of-face contrast (Bodoni's stroke modulation against Manrope's even sans), and color drop (ink → `--soul-muted`) — not from boxes or backgrounds. One eyebrow token (`text-[0.7rem] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.28em]`, page.tsx:34) is defined once and reused everywhere, giving the small caps a consistent voice. Body copy is leashed to `max-w-md` / `max-w-sm` for line length; the H1 is manually broken with `
` into three one-word lines so it never rags.
color: Seven tokens, scoped to `.page` in soul.module.css:15-27 rather than the global theme (with the reason written in the file: four demo palettes in one `@theme` would ship every studio's tokens on every page). Ground is `--soul-bone #f4eee8`, a warm paper; ink is `--soul-ink #171411`, a warm near-black, never pure #000. The accent is split into a documented two-tier pair — `--soul-clay #b86f5c` annotated \"3.3:1 on bone — display sizes and rules only\" and `--soul-clay-deep #8f4a39` annotated \"5.7:1 — anything set small in the accent colour.\" That single decision is why all the little uppercase kickers, the CTA fill, and the header outline button stay legible while the big italic \"Prisustvo.\" gets the lighter, prettier tone. Deployment is stingy: color appears as one word in the H1, the six eyebrows, one filled CTA, the clay hairlines above each practice, and the sticky dock. Exactly one tinted band exists — `--soul-sand #eae0d6` behind the motto section (page.tsx:204) — so the page's emotional center is marked by a ground change that happens once, instead of the usual alternating-section stripes. Two line weights, `--soul-line` for structure and `--soul-line-clay` for the two practice rules, are the only borders on the page.
composition: Header (page.tsx:67-103): a single hairline-bottom bar, wordmark in Bodoni left, letterspaced caps nav center, and one outlined clay pill right. No sticky, no shadow, no blur — it scrolls away and the mobile dock takes over.

Hero (109-167): asymmetric `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_0.85fr]` with `lg:items-end` — text column and arch bottom-align, which is what makes the arch look seated on the baseline rather than floating. Reading order is inverted on mobile via `order-1/order-2` so the photograph greets the phone first and the headline follows. Vertical stack inside the left rail: H1 → hairline → signature → paragraph → two buttons → address, each with a different top margin (mt-4/6/9/8), so spacing carries rhythm rather than uniform gaps.

Prakse (171-201): the anti-card move. Two long-form articles side by side, separated only by a clay hairline above each, with `md:gap-x-16` and no boxes at all. Each has three text weights — kicker, Bodoni title at text-4xl/5xl, body at ink, note at muted — so a comparison happens through typography instead of two matching tiles.

Pristup (204-237): the density peak. Left column is small (0.9fr) and quiet — kicker, H2, one explanatory paragraph capped at max-w-sm; right column (1.1fr) is `content-center` and holds three enormous Bodoni lines. The section's ground changes to sand, the type gets bigger than the H2 that introduced it, and the visual weight sits hard right — the single most confident composition on the page.

Prostor (241-287): `lg:grid-cols-[0.85fr_1.15fr]` with the text column `lg:sticky lg:top-8` so the story stays put while the four-frame uneven gallery scrolls past it. The comment states the intent — "so the text never sits alone in a full-width column."

Kontakt (289-347): the street address is promoted to the H2 ("Crnogorskih Serdara 45") and the <address> below deliberately carries only the city, with a comment explaining that printing the full address again read as the same sentence twice. Map occupies the right half as an unloaded plate.
Footer (350-366): `sm:items-end sm:justify-between` — wordmark and disclaimer left, credit line baseline-aligned right. No columns of links, no repeated nav, no newsletter.
interaction: Scroll-driven CSS only (soul.module.css:37-51): `animation-timeline: view()` with tuned ranges (`entry 8% cover 38%` for the photo uncover, `entry 15% cover 40%` for the rule draw). Zero JS, zero observers, and the un-animated fallback state is the correct finished page. Earns its place — two gestures, both metaphorically tied to the room (light crossing the floor; a line being drawn).

Hover is color-only, everywhere: `transition-colors` on nav links, both CTAs, the header pill, and the phone pill. No translate, no scale, no shadow lift — consistent with the house ban and correct for a calm brand.

Focus is a single shared token (page.tsx:35-36): `focus-visible:outline-2 outline-offset-4` in clay-deep, appended to every interactive class string including the dock (which flips to `offset-[-4px]` in bone so the ring stays inside the filled cell). Genuinely thorough — the footer credit link and the Instagram arrow link both carry it.

Click-to-load map (MapEmbed.tsx): a real <button> gates the Google iframe, with a plain "Otvori u Google Mapama" link that costs no request at all as the always-available fallback. Privacy and performance in one control; the only stateful component on the page.

Sticky story column on desktop (`lg:sticky lg:top-8`) — the one persistent-position element, and it does real work: it keeps the studio's origin story readable while its evidence (the photos) scrolls.
Touch targets are enforced numerically rather than assumed: `min-h-11` on every text link (including the wordmark and the footer credit), `min-h-12` on CTAs, `min-h-14` on both dock cells.
mobile: At 390px the page reflows into a single narrow editorial column and holds because the hierarchy was never carried by the grid. The arch photo moves above the headline (`order-1`), so the first thing on screen is the room; the H1's `9vw` clamp keeps \"Pokret. / Disanje. / Prisustvo.\" at genuine display scale instead of shrinking to a subhead. The motto section survives best — the three Bodoni lines at `6vw` still dominate their band. The uneven gallery collapses to a straight stack of four photos of varying heights (`aspect-[4/5]`, `h-56`, `h-56`, `h-56`), which reads as a slideshow of the room rather than a broken grid. Desktop nav is dropped entirely (`hidden md:flex`) and replaced by the fixed pill dock, whose asymmetric split gives the Instagram cell room for a two-line label with a truncated handle while Pozovi stays a compact icon+word; the dock sits above the home indicator via `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and the page reserves matching bottom padding so the footer is never occluded. All CTAs go `flex-col` full-width, and every body block was already `max-w-md`, so nothing needs to reflow to stay readable.

transferableIdeas.idea: Borrow one physical geometry from the client's own premises and make it the page's single exception to an otherwise flat rule.
transferableIdeas.why: The arch crop is unarguably *this* studio's — you can see the same arch inside the photograph it frames. Because it is the only rounded thing on the page, it functions as a logo without being one, and every square edge elsewhere becomes a deliberate contrast rather than a default. This is the difference between a decorated page and a designed one.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Scan the client's photos for one repeated shape: a bakery's oven mouth, a barber's mirror, a garage's roller-shutter slats, a winery's barrel end, a hotel's balcony arcade. Apply it to exactly one element (a photo crop, a section top edge, a button) and forbid it everywhere else on the page.

transferableIdeas.idea: Set the client's own physical lettering as the largest typography on the page, and say in the copy that it is theirs.
transferableIdeas.why: The motto section is the page's peak because the words are not marketing — they are painted on the wall, photographed two sections later, and the surrounding sentence explicitly declines to call them a slogan. Copy the business already stands behind cannot read as AI-generated, and giving it more scale than your own H2 is a genuine act of art direction.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Photograph or transcribe what is already written in the space — the chalkboard, the neon, the van door, the menu header, the family motto on the receipt — and give it its own band at display size. Frame it with one honest line about where it comes from, never with a quote mark and an author byline.

transferableIdeas.idea: Invert the eyebrow: put the category descriptor *below* the H1 under a hairline, as a signature.
transferableIdeas.why: The badge-above-heading opener is the single most recognizable AI-landing-page tell. Moving the same words underneath costs nothing, changes the reading order from label-then-claim to claim-then-attribution, and makes the H1 the true first mark on the page.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Works on any page: `<h1>` → hairline → `Category · City` in the small-caps token → body → CTAs. Applies unchanged to a law firm, a bakery, a garage.

transferableIdeas.idea: Replace a features grid with two long-form blocks written *against each other*, answering the one question a first-time customer actually has.
transferableIdeas.why: practices[] in data.ts is a comparison, not a benefits list — its comment states the job outright: "let someone who has never done either tell the two apart." Each block carries a body paragraph plus a distinct `note` about what it feels like in the room. It is more useful than six icon cards and structurally cannot look like them.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Identify the client's genuine either/or (dry-aged vs. fresh, gel vs. acrylic, kompletna vs. djelimična renovacija, degustacija vs. ručak) and build one section of exactly two prose blocks, separated only by a rule, with the smaller closing line reserved for the honest practical difference.

transferableIdeas.idea: Drive an asymmetric photo layout from a map keyed by content id, not array index.
transferableIdeas.why: GALLERY_LAYOUT (page.tsx:44-49) plus `as const satisfies readonly Photo[]` means the tall frame, the two stacked squares, and the wide closer are bound to specific photographs — TypeScript rejects a stale key, so the deliberate unevenness survives someone adding or reordering a photo. Most asymmetric grids are hand-tuned and silently degrade on the first content edit; this one doesn't.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Any gallery, any business: `Record<Photo['src'], { cell: string; box: string }>` with span/height per image, chosen from the photos' real aspect ratios. Give the most content-rich frame the largest cell.

transferableIdeas.idea: Two gestures of scroll-driven motion, in pure CSS, both metaphorically tied to the subject — with the un-animated state as the correct page.
transferableIdeas.why: `animation-timeline: view()` behind `@supports` and `prefers-reduced-motion` gives motion at zero JS and zero risk: no observer, no hydration, and a browser without support shows a finished page rather than invisible content. Capping it at two gestures is what keeps it from becoming the banned scattered scroll-reveal.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Pick two motions the business physically performs — dough rising (bottom-up clip-path), a shutter lifting, a saw cut travelling (scaleX rule), a curtain parting — and bind them to `view()` with tuned `animation-range`. Never animate every child; never animate text blocks.

transferableIdeas.idea: Split the accent color into a display tier and a small-text tier, and write the contrast ratios into the CSS as comments.
transferableIdeas.why: `--soul-clay` at 3.3:1 is the pretty terracotta that makes the italic "Prisustvo." sing; `--soul-clay-deep` at 5.7:1 carries every kicker, the CTA fill, and the header outline. One token would have forced a choice between a washed-out accent and illegible small type. The annotations mean the next developer cannot misuse them by accident.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: For any brand color: define `--x` (large/decorative) and `--x-deep` (anything under ~24px or bearing text), measure both against the ground, and comment the ratios in the token block. Costs one line, prevents the most common accessibility failure in branded pages.

transferableIdeas.idea: Change the ground exactly once, at the page's emotional center, instead of alternating section backgrounds.
transferableIdeas.why: The sand band under the motto is the only background change in the document, so it reads as emphasis rather than as rhythm-filler. Alternating white/grey sections is the visual equivalent of shouting every third sentence.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Choose the single section that is the reason someone would trust this business — the signature dish, the guarantee, the founder's line — and give only that one a tinted ground, kept within a couple of steps of the base so it reads as paper, not as a panel.

transferableIdeas.idea: Scope the whole palette to a route-level CSS module class, with the reason written down.
transferableIdeas.why: soul.module.css defines all seven tokens on `.page` rather than in the global `@theme`, so four demo brands coexist without shipping each other's tokens site-wide, while Tailwind's scanner still resolves `bg-[var(--soul-bone)]` because those are literal class strings. It is a real architectural decision, explained in three lines.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Any multi-brand or multi-demo repo: one CSS module per brand exposing custom properties on a wrapper class; components reference `var(--token)` through arbitrary-value utilities and stay brand-agnostic.

transferableIdeas.idea: Write the content file as a provenance contract that states what must NOT be added.
transferableIdeas.why: data.ts opens by naming the source (the studio's public Instagram, with the date it was read) and explicitly listing what is absent and forbidden until confirmed: schedule, prices, the announced second location, any health claim. That constraint is why the page contains no fake stats, no invented testimonials, and no filler — the anti-slop outcome is enforced upstream of the design.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Head every demo/client data module with source, read-date, and a do-not-invent list. Then design only for what's actually there; the layout is forced to earn its interest from composition rather than from padding.

transferableIdeas.idea: Give the mobile action bar a shape, not a full-bleed strip.
transferableIdeas.why: An inset pill with an asymmetric two-cell split, a solid ground, and a shadow that only lifts it — plus a two-line label so the primary action shows the actual Instagram handle — reads as part of the design system (it echoes the arch and the rounded CTAs) instead of an appended widget. Matching page-bottom padding means the footer never hides under it.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Reuse the pattern for any local business: primary channel gets the wider filled cell with a micro-label over the identifier (handle, phone, "Rezerviši"), secondary gets the narrow outlined cell. Always pair with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and matching body padding.

weaknesses: The letterspaced uppercase kicker is used six times (hero signature, both practices, Pristup, Prostor, Dolazak) and is always paired with a hairline rule. That combination *is* the "AI editorial broadsheet" grammar the house standard bans. Soul escapes it only because the arch and the wall motto are strong enough to carry the identity — the kicker is not doing the work, it is riding along. Do not transfer the kicker+hairline pair as a default section opener; on a page without an equally strong signature element it collapses straight into the rejected style.

The Prakse section is the weakest thing on desktop. Two text-only columns whose `max-w-md` copy is narrower than its grid cell leaves a ragged, apparently accidental right gutter in each half, and the section has no photograph, no scale contrast beyond the H3, and no visual anchor — after the arch hero it reads as a drop in production value rather than as intentional quiet.

The arch breaks at 390px. `rounded-t-[14rem]` against a `h-52` (13rem) box means the radius exceeds the height, so the browser clamps it and the arch collapses into a half-round lozenge — the signature element is at its weakest precisely on the viewport where most visitors will see it, and the lit arch inside the photo gets cropped out of the frame too.

The map plate is a large dead rectangle. On desktop it is a full grid column of faint grey graph paper; on phone it is a 288px-tall empty box near the bottom of the page. The privacy logic is right, but the placeholder should carry something — the address, a drawn approach, a neighborhood note — rather than a note about Google's servers.

The phone number rendered as an outlined pill (page.tsx:307-315) reads as a disabled chip or a form field rather than a tap target; it is visually identical to the secondary CTA but sits alone in a text block with no verb.

The photographs are raw Instagram frames and they fight the palette: colour temperature swings from the warm yellow arch to cool blue-grey reformers, and the wide closing frame is dominated by a bright blue exercise ball that is the most saturated object on an otherwise bone-and-clay page. A calm palette needs a graded photo set; this one is inherited.

No mobile navigation at all — the four section anchors are simply `hidden md:flex`, and the dock replaces them with two contact actions. Defensible for a short one-page concept, but it is a dropped feature, not a mobile design; on a longer page it would be a real failure.

The sticky story column in Prostor leaves a tall empty area on desktop once the copy runs out while the gallery keeps scrolling. Deliberate negative space is fine, but here the left rail simply stops, and the void is larger than any intentional whitespace elsewhere on the page.

`--soul-clay` at 3.3:1 sets the italic "Prisustvo." — the third line of the H1. It passes at display size, but the page's most important word is also its lightest, which is a hierarchy inversion the design gets away with rather than one it exploits.
